lessons.title: Why animals need food and water
lessons.html:
Food keeps animals alive and productive

Animals eat to stay alive, to grow, to work, to make milk, wool, meat and eggs, and to have young. If an animal does not get enough of the right food it loses weight, gets sick more easily and produces less. Good feeding is one of the biggest costs on a farm, so it must be done well.

The main nutrients

NutrientWhat it doesExamples
WaterMost important of all. Cools the body, carries food, makes milkClean drinking water
Energy (carbohydrates and fats)Gives power to move, keep warm and growMaize, molasses, green grass
ProteinBuilds muscle, milk, wool and young animalsLucerne, oilcake, legumes
MineralsStrong bones, teeth and good healthSalt, phosphate licks
VitaminsHelp the body work properlyGreen feed, supplements

Water first

An animal can live for weeks without food but only a few days without water. Check troughs every day. Water must be clean, cool and always available. Clean troughs often and fix leaking pipes and floats quickly. In hot weather animals drink much more.

Signs of poor feeding

  • Animals are thin and you can see ribs and hip bones clearly.
  • Dull, rough coat or poor wool.
  • Animals chew bones, wood or soil. This can mean they lack minerals such as phosphorus.
  • Low milk, slow growth, cows not coming on heat.

Report these signs to your supervisor.

lessons.title: How different animals digest food
lessons.html:
Ruminants

Cattle, sheep and goats are ruminants. They have a stomach with four parts. The biggest part is the rumen. Inside the rumen live millions of tiny microbes that break down grass, hay and other rough feed. That is why ruminants can live on veld grass that people and pigs cannot use.

  • Ruminants chew the cud. They bring food back up and chew it again while resting.
  • If a cow or sheep stops chewing the cud, it may be sick. Tell your supervisor.
  • Sudden changes in feed upset the rumen microbes. Change feed slowly over about two weeks.
  • Too much grain eaten too fast can cause acidosis and bloat, which can kill. Keep feed stores locked so animals cannot break in.

Monogastric animals

Pigs and chickens have one simple stomach, like people. They cannot use much grass. They need feed with more grain and protein, such as maize meal, soya and fish meal, usually as a balanced ration bought from a feed company.

Horses

Horses have a simple stomach but a large hind gut that digests grass and hay. They need good hay or grazing and should not get sudden large amounts of grain.

Grazing and veld

In summer the veld is green and has good protein. In winter the grass is dry and low in protein. Many farmers give a protein lick in winter and a phosphate lick in summer. Your manager will decide which lick to use. Always follow the instructions on the bag.

lessons.title: Feeding animals correctly every day
lessons.html:
Daily feeding tasks

  1. Check water troughs first.
  2. Give the right feed to the right group, in the right amount, at the same time each day.
  3. Spread feed so that weak animals also get a chance to eat.
  4. Watch how the animals eat. Animals that do not come to eat may be sick.
  5. Clean feed troughs. Remove wet, mouldy or old feed.
  6. Write down what was fed and any problems.

Storing feed

  • Keep bags off the floor on pallets, in a dry, closed store.
  • Keep rats, birds and dogs out. Rats spoil feed and spread disease.
  • Use old stock first.
  • Never feed mouldy feed. Mould can make animals very sick.
  • Keep poisons, dips and fertiliser far away from feed.

Dangerous feeding mistakes

  • Urea: some licks contain urea. Too much urea kills ruminants quickly. Never give urea licks to pigs or horses. Mix and give exactly as the label says.
  • Chicken litter and feed for other animals: do not give feed made for one kind of animal to another kind unless your manager says so. Some feeds are poisonous to other animals.
  • Sudden change: do not suddenly let hungry animals into green lucerne or a maize land. They can bloat.

If an animal is blown up on the left side, is in pain or falls down, call your supervisor and the vet at once.

Key points

  • Clean water must always be available.
  • Animals need energy, protein, minerals, vitamins and water.
  • Ruminants digest grass in the rumen; change their feed slowly.
  • Never feed mouldy feed and store feed dry and away from poisons.
  • Give urea licks only as the label says and never to pigs or horses.
